lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?

lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear you're going through this.

lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our systems are not responding right now.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.

unsupported_rules: `no_promise` | `refused` | no promise recorded, one or more products refused (3.4), any others disputed or paid — the brief ranks refused above dispute/paid on multi-product calls regardless of account order; the engine uses the first product's ending in account order.
`no_promise` | `service_error` | 7.6, or no promise recorded because of a 3.5 failure — ranking of service_error against other product endings when no promise is recorded is not expressible.

quotes: That opening question is counted as the first proposal and uses up one unit of the product's persuasion limit.
If a rung has the same amount and the same date as something already proposed for that product, including the opening question, leave it out.
A rung that is left out is not counted as a proposal and does not use up the limit; move straight on to the following rung.
If the customer says the amount is too much, the very next proposal you make is the floor.
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: The floor becomes the next proposal and, like any proposal, uses an attempt; the brief gives no special date, so the default attempt_1 is kept.

rules.too_much_skips_full.assumption: Later full-amount rungs are not skipped automatically; only exact repeats are skipped (3.3).

quotes: Proposing ends as soon as the product's persuasion limit has been reached or there are no rungs left, whichever happens first.
After each flat refusal (a no that comes with neither a date nor an amount), go down one rung
rules.refuse_deadline_is_refusal.derivation: A plain no to a deadline-dated proposal is a flat refusal and moves down a rung.

quotes: If `create_promise` fails two times, note `service_error` for that product.

Customer is in financial hardship (lost job, illness, bereavement): express sympathy in a single sentence, make no proposals, note `hardship` on every product not yet handled, and close `no_promise` / `hardship`.
rules.hardship_transfer.derivation: Sympathy in one sentence and no question or offer; no support transfer exists (transfer_support queue empty), so the call closes with the hardship event.

quotes: Only after that step, if the resulting date is not a business day, push it forward to the following business day.
On each product the agent's first question is: "Can you pay the full overdue amount of EUR {amount} today?"

rules.week_end_today.assumption: No week-end ladder step is used; read literally.

quotes: for an overdraft, `overdue_eur` divided by four and rounded up to a whole euro (no rounding when the quarter is already a whole euro amount); when `overdue_eur` is less than 100, the floor equals the full overdue amount.
products.floor_pct.derivation: Divided by four = 25 percent of overdue_eur, for overdrafts only.

products.floor_min.assumption: No minimum floor beyond the overdraft under-100 rule.

quotes: when `overdue_eur` is less than 100, the floor equals the full overdue amount.
for an overdraft, `overdue_eur` divided by four and rounded up to a whole euro (no rounding when the quarter is already a whole euro amount)
half of the overdue amount rounded up to a whole euro (left as is when already a whole euro), dated on the deadline; when that is lower than the floor, the floor takes its place;
The amount sent to `create_promise` is an integer number of euro cents (for EUR 45.10, send 4510).

products.promise_round.assumption: Euro amounts with cents convert exactly to cents; no rounding rule is given.

quotes: From 4 November 2026 onwards (calls on that date or later), the `close_call` reason `hardship` is replaced with `financial_difficulty`; the outcome remains `no_promise`.

assumptions: Brief 5.2 (verification ends at the second incorrect answer) overrides the API summary (three wrong answers): max_wrong = 2.
Opening wording: the brief prescribes 'This call is recorded.'; per the format rules it is spoken in active voice as 'We record this call.'
ask_today: the brief's 'EUR {amount}' became '{amount}' because the engine's {amount} already includes the currency word.
The brief has no title variable, so confirm_ask uses {first_name} {last_name}, as 6.1 asks.

Ladder step 1 is the opening ask (full amount today) because the opening counts as proposal 1. The rungs are full/deadline, 50% rounded up to a whole euro (never below the floor)/deadline, then floor/deadline. Tier 1 allows 2 proposals and Tier 2 allows 3, both counting the opening.
Overdraft floor = 25% of overdue_eur rounded up to a whole euro. If overdue_eur < 100, the floor is the full overdue amount. Card floor = min_due_eur, loan floor = monthly_instalment_eur.

Tier 2 deadline: the 15th of this month, rolled to next month's 15th only when it is earlier than today (on the 15th the deadline is today). After the roll, a non-business day moves forward to the next business day. Tier 1 deadline = the 6th business day after today, never a non-business day.
deadline_adjust = next_business_day, from 4.3 (push forward) and 4.4 (offer the following business day).
Hardship: the brief prescribes no support transfer, so transfer_support has no queue and mirrors the hardship close code. The hardship line is a single sentence of sympathy.
The memo OPS-26-31 hardship -> financial_difficulty change applies from 2026-11-04 as an event_change. The add_note reason stays 'hardship'.
Callback window 09:30-18:00 inclusive, today or the next business day, after now, two attempts. business_days_only is not stated, so it is false.
The brief is silent on how 'next <weekday>' is read; the default following_week is used.
The brief is silent on max_unclear, max_not_talk, purpose_is_decline, ask_anything_else and changing a recorded promise; defaults are used, and promise_change says it cannot be changed on this call.
A date of birth spoken as numbers only is read day-month-year (date_order dmy) and sent as YYYY-MM-DD.
Below-floor line avoids the word 'recorded' (format rule); it says the amount can't be accepted, then the floor is proposed once.
bands_outside is not stated by the brief (it covers 1-60 days only); the default service_error is used.
promise_round is left null: overdue and floor amounts are whole cents and convert exactly with promise_scale 100.
